# Clem

> A calm, local-first Windows workspace for projects, study and documents, powered by the AI plan you already have. Free and open source (MIT), from M4 Labs.

Clem is one quiet place for the work you bring to an AI: a course, a research question, a report, a pile of PDFs. Instead of another chat tab, you get subjects and projects that hold your files, chats, flashcards and drafts together, and an AI that answers from them.

- Yours, on your PC: everything lives in `Documents\Clem` as plain files. No lock-in, no upload of your library.
- Bring your own AI: connect the ChatGPT, Claude, Grok or Google AI (Antigravity) plan you already pay for. Clem adds no subscription.
- Free and open source: no plan, no trial, no card.

Clem is a preview: most of it is used daily, but some flows are still being verified.

## What it does

- Study that sticks: subjects collect your notes and slides; Clem makes flashcards, quizzes and worksheets from them and schedules every card with FSRS spaced repetition, paced to your exam date.
- Real documents: typeset PDFs, or real Word, PowerPoint and Excel files. Edits change the same file, with Before/After and Undo.
- Answers you can check: citations open your file at the right page; calculations end with a check block Clem recomputes; any answer can get a second opinion from another model.
- Visuals for any idea: `/visual` and a topic gives interactive plots, 3D surfaces, step-through diagrams and charts, exportable to PNG, SVG or PDF.
- Your folders, live: link folders on your PC or in Google Drive; Clem reads them in place and proposes edits as diffs you approve.
- Long tasks: multi-step work, chats side by side, and moving to another connected account when one runs low on usage.
- Proactivity: a main thread where Clem plans your day, turns deadlines into tasks and sends updates in Clem, as Windows notifications or on Telegram.
- GUC (German University in Cairo) connector: course files, announcements, grades and deadlines, saved on a schedule you describe in plain words.
